description.narrative: Masarouna mobilizes the power of young people in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) so they can claim their sexual and reproductive health and rights. We work with and for young people, and together we forge new pathways to create meaningful and sustainable change. Masarouna is a 5-year program funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs

owner-org.narrative: The activity is under Massarouna project funded by Oxfam

activity-date.narrative: Fe-Male has started the implementation since August 2022

provider-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib has provided the fund

description.narrative: EO2 Young people have increased knowledge and skills to claim their SRHR

KI-7a # Gender not specified young people reached with comprehensive, correct information on SRHR for diverse young people, facilitated by Masarouna (not including young people reached via social media only)

comment.narrative: NA

For participants whose gender is not specified, the SRHR information sessions provided by FEMALE are particularly significant. With a focus on engaging 20 young people with gender not specified , the aim is to create an environment where their unique experiences and concerns are acknowledged and respected. These sessions provide a platform for open dialogue and discussion, fostering a supportive atmosphere where they can feel comfortable addressing their SRHR-related questions and needs.
The strategic partner's Academy, previously known a Bootcamp, will deliver 35 training workshops targeting 15 individuals each in 2024, among which an estimated 175 young people (gender not specified). These training sessions will educate and engage individuals on the basics of SRHR and its derivatives, fostering a more inclusive and informed community. 3 training modules, namely SRHR for Mental Health Professionals, SRHR1 and SRHR2 will be developed. SRHR material, developed in 2023 and 2024 within the framework of the Academy will be digitized, aiming to serve as online training modules.
200 young people whose gender is not specified will be reached by Oxfam through a combination of social media and other means such as round tables, trainings, peer-to-peer trainings, capacity building, awareness sessions and national conferences on SRHR. The program seeks to enable youth to have greater freedom over their SRHR and contribute to changes in norms, behaviors and attitudes when it come to SRHR. The exact topics of the information shared ill be decided after assessing the capacity needs and context.

Between June and August 2024, Oxfam's partner program provided 6 remote awareness raising sessions to diverse young people, from diverse healthcare backgrounds including nursing and midwifery and social work on various topics, including adolescent development, consent, and inclusive care. 1 young person whose gender was not specified attended. Pre and post tests were conducted in order to assess the improvement in knowledge of the participants. The average result showed 10% improvement in their knowledge on the various SRHR topics provided. FEMALE reached approximately 60 young people whose gender was not specified through SRHR awareness sessions (excluding the youth trajectory bootcamp), including around 18 under 18; 30 aged 18–35; and 12 aged above 35 years old. Finally, In 2024, 25 trainings were conducted by the Strategic Partner for 271 participants on SRHR concepts, protection mechanisms, and community organizing. Due to the volatile context, the online modules developed under their Academy in 2023–2024 remain unavailable. While the SRHR materials were digitized into self-paced learning modules, final revisions and enhancements have been delayed and are now scheduled for completion in 2025, with the course set to launch on their website. This delay also contributed to the gap between the 2024 targets and actual achievements. Among the participants, there were an estimated 75 whose gender was not specified under 35 years old.

Fe-Male will conduct around 36 SRHR information sessions in safe spaces for youth, around 10% of them will be young people whose gender is not specified. Masarouna’s strategic partner will organise a bootcamp, which will consist of 24 training workshops targeting 15 individuals each in 2023. The aim of the bootcamp is to provide accurate and updated knowledge in an engaging and simplified format about SRHR to young people, service providers and staff of CSOs. The total target (360 individuals) include an estimated 30 members of CSOs, 30 service providers and 300 young people. The numeric target of the online version of the bootcamp is set at 20 individuals.

In 2023, multiple awareness raising sessions were conducted by FEMALE in different regions, most of them in FEMALE's marginalized centers. Topics covered were SRHR and GBV in different methods talking about laws, rights, health throughout multiple methodologies (art, discussions, presentations). Among the young people we reached, there were 4 young people whose gender was not specified.
Through targeted training programs conducted by the strategic partner, a diverse group of young people experienced significant growth in understanding and affirming diversity and inclusion. Among them, marginalized youth have been empowered with tailored programs focusing on self-acceptance, advocacy skills, and support networks, while their allies have gained knowledge in creating inclusive environments and combating discrimination. These efforts have not only elevated their awareness but also fostered a sense of solidarity and allyship among the youth. (Among the young people reached in 2023, there were 31 young people whose gender was not specified)
Towards the end of 2023, Oxfam in country selected a consultant to collaborate with young people to develop an SRHR glossary document aiming to provide accessible comprehensive and correct information on SRHR for diverse young people and young people with visual and hearing disabilities. The SRHR glossary is expected to be finalised by mid 2024. Moreover, Oxfam partners and subgrantees will conduct awareness raising sessions to divers YP providing comprehensive and correct information on SRHR during 2024. As a result, actual reporting by Oxfam on KI-7a is expected to start in 2024.
In total, 35 young people who gender was not specified were reached with comprehensive, correct SRHR information by Masarouna partners in 2023, against a target of 160 for 2023.
Fe-Male will organise around 16 information sessions with youth. Around 10% of them will be young people with gender not specified.

Oxfam started in 2022 to develop the 2023 implementation plan, that will cover activities aiming at changing behaviors and attitudes of young people's SRHR, including initiatives that provide correct and evidence based information on SRHR for diverse young people.
A total of 16 awareness sessions about SRHR were conducted in four regions at Fe-Male's centers in 2022, reaching a total of 262 attendees, among which 229 young people. The total number of the young people whose gender was not specified who had participated in the 16 awareness raising sessions was 11, less than the estimated target of 25 young people for 2022. Among the 11 young people whose gender was not specified reached in 2022, 8 are nationals and 3 are refugees. . The sessions are being provided in innovative and interactive methodologies with advanced trainers who are well equipped and knowledgable about SRHR to provide accurrate information. The topics included period poverty,sexual reproductive health, and stigma and sexually transmitted diseases. The sessions had a great impact represented through the satisfaction surveys that were filled by the participants, in addition to the results in the Pre-Post tests that showed increase in the percentage of knowledge after the sessions.

The program seeks to enable youth to have greater freedom over their SRHR and contribute to changes in norms, behaviours and attitudes when it comes to SRHR. 40 young people whose gender has not been specified will be reached by Oxfam and partners in 2025 through other means than social media, through capacity building and awareness sessions on SRHR topics. The topics will be related to SRHR for young people. The Strategic Partner's Academy plans to conduct a total of 20 training sessions, covering four key SRHR modules. Each session will target a minimum of 5 and a maximum of 15 participants. Participant disaggregation data will not be available until the reporting period, allowing for a more comprehensive analysis of attendance and engagement at that time. The estimated no. of young people whose gender is not specified in these sessions in 2025 is 25. In 2024, SRHR materials developed under the Strategic Partner's Academy framework in 2023 and 2024 underwent digitization to create comprehensive online training modules. These modules are designed to provide accessible, self-paced learning for a wider audience. Final revisions and enhancements will be completed in 2025, with the online course set to be available on the Strategic Partner's website

description.narrative: LTO 1: Decision-makers have formulated (and implemented where possible) policies, and/or removed/amended harmful policies, to enable young people to enjoy their SRHR.
KI-1a # Laws blocked, adopted and/or improved to enable diverse young people to enjoy their SRHR

comment.narrative: NA

Update Oct. 2023: By 2025, FEMALE will have significantly increased awareness about the importance of digital security law and online sexual harassment reporting. This will be measured by the level of engagement and support from key stakeholders, including government officials, civil society organizations, and the public. However, in the short timeframe it is hard to change the law due to the other ongoing conflicts in the country and the region and the pending priorities of the government, which is why the quantitative 5-year target has been adjusted from 1 to zero at mid term.
Considering the current unstable situation in the country (political, backlash, security), Oxfam may be unable to achieve the initially planned target of ''1'' law blocked, adopted and/or improved. Therefore we have changed this target to zero. Throughout the remaining 2 years of implementation, we will try to progress towards such change, but are unsure to achieve actual law change.
The consolidated 5-year target was adjusted from 1 to 0 laws at midterm, based on the adjustments made by consortium partners
